overview: After 2.Nc3 e6 White plays 3.d4 and Black hits the centre with ...d5, reaching a French-Tarrasch or Sicilian hybrid with an IQP-type structure. White can play 4.exd5 exd5 5.Nf3 with a tarrasch-like game or 4.e5 for a French Advance with an extra Nc3. Black's c5 pawn may be taken (dxc5), the source of the 'gambit' name, but Black normally regains it.

white_ideas.idea: Play exd5 exd5 and Nf3, Bb5 and castle, putting pressure on the isolated d5 pawn.
Advance with e5 for a space edge and attack the c5 pawn.

black_ideas.idea: Support the centre with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6 and play for active pieces and the IQP.
Take d4 with ...cxd4 to open the centre and attack the knight on c3.

typical_structures.structure: Tarrasch-like isolated queen's pawn for Black, or a French Advance structure after e5.

character.notes: Strategic with an isolated pawn or tension; I am not sure of the main theory.

gambit.notes: Any pawn on c5 is usually regained, so no lasting gambit in the main branch.

soundness.notes: Playable; I am unsure of the exact assessment.

structure.notes: Tarrasch-like asymmetric centre with half-open files.

approach.notes: A rare mix of Sicilian and French; strong players seldom choose it.

level.notes: Needs understanding of IQP and French structures.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.e5
sublines_that_differ.how: A French Advance-type position with White space.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.dxc5
sublines_that_differ.how: White takes the pawn and Black regains it with ...d4 and ...Bxc5.

character.reason: Strategic tension with no clear forcing line.

gambit.reason: Material usually returns; main line has none given.

plans.reason: Black's d5 pawn becomes isolated after exchanges.
